hackathon_name: Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 4: Ghost in the Machine

primitives.name: dev.to (DEV) as submission platform
primitives.can: Markdown post with cover image, tables, code blocks, embedded GIF/video, liquid embeds (GitHub repo card, {% agent_session %}); tags gate the submission; reactions are the published tiebreaker
primitives.cant: Cannot host a running app; no originality auto-check (manual judging); theme page kept secret until launch so exact prompt text is only on the live page
primitives.evidence: dev.to challenge page + Week 1 contest rules + munim winner study
primitives.load_bearing_for: THE submission itself — the post is the product; writing quality is the single heaviest judged axis

primitives.name: Render (web service hosting)
primitives.can: Deploy a public web service / Docker container; host the agent frontend + OSS AI runtime; qualifies for Best Use of Render ($200)
primitives.cant: FREE tier spins down after 15 min idle (first post-sleep request 30-60s); 512MB/0.1CPU free is too small for local LLM weights; 750 free instance-hrs/mo then suspended
primitives.evidence: agentdeals.dev/vendor/render + temps.sh render-pricing-2026 (free sleeps; Starter $7/mo always-on 512MB; $25/mo 2GB)
primitives.load_bearing_for: Best Use of Render ($200) + the live demo link — MUST be a durable paid tier (Starter $7/mo min) so it is up during the judging window (dl-1 ephemeral-infra-dies lesson)

primitives.name: Groq free API (hosted open-weight inference)
primitives.can: OpenAI-compatible hosted inference for OPEN-WEIGHT models (Llama 3.1/3.3, Qwen3-32B); fastest TTFB (~85ms) + 280-660 tok/s; free tier no credit card; trivial to call from a tiny Render service
primitives.cant: Rate-limited free tier (30-60 RPM, 6-12k TPM) — fine for a demo, not production load; it is hosted (not local), so lean on 'open-weight model' framing, not 'local inference'
primitives.load_bearing_for: the open-source-AI CORE via a Render-friendly path — keeps the Render service tiny (no GPU/weights to host), satisfies the open-weight requirement, fast enough to demo live

primitives.name: Ollama + small open-weight model (local inference)
primitives.can: Run Gemma 2/3, Qwen 2.5, Phi-4-mini fully locally/offline; strongest 'open innovation' + 'local inference' narrative; the dominant stack among current competitors
primitives.cant: Even a 2-4B Q4 model needs ~2-4GB RAM — exceeds Render free (512MB) and Starter (512MB); needs $25/mo 2GB tier at least, or ship it local-only and deploy only a thin UI; Render cold-pull of weights is slow
primitives.load_bearing_for: the 'offline / privacy / local-first' narrative axis — load-bearing ONLY if the build stays local or buys a 2GB+ Render tier; otherwise Groq carries the core and Ollama is a mentioned local-dev path

primitives.name: TabPFN-3.5 (Prior Labs tabular foundation model)
primitives.can: pip install tabpfn (local, open weights on HF, non-commercial) OR tabpfn-client (hosted API, GPU-managed); one checkpoint does classification + regression in a forward pass; zero training; qualifies for Best Use of TabPFN ($200)
primitives.cant: Needs TABULAR historical data to be natural — no native fit for text/story generation; local weights are non-commercial-license + GPU-friendly (heavy for Render free); license acceptance step (interactive login) adds a build-time wrinkle
primitives.load_bearing_for: Best Use of TabPFN ($200) — load-bearing ONLY for a concept with a genuine tabular-prediction core; flagged NOT-load-bearing for a pure story/chat build (would be a bolt-on = penalized)

primitives.name: DevRelay (agent-session embed)
primitives.can: Embed an AI coding-agent transcript via {% agent_session id %}; shows the judges your build process; organizer explicitly says judges appreciate it
primitives.cant: Optional, not scored directly; capturing a clean session needs Cursor+DevRelay or the devrelay CLI mid-build (must plan to capture during the build, not after)
primitives.load_bearing_for: NOT load-bearing — a free credibility/transparency boost in the post; capture opportunistically during build
